chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And for the divorced women is provision in a fair manner, a duty upon the righteous.'
He said: 'Her provision is after her waiting period ends, according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor.'
And he said: 'How can he provide for her during her waiting period when she hopes for him and he hopes for her, and Allah may bring about whatever He wills?'
Indeed, the wealthy man provides for the woman with a male or female slave, and the poor man provides with wheat, raisins, clothing, and dirhams.
And indeed, Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) provided for a woman he divorced with a female slave, and he did not divorce a woman without providing for her.

key_terms.الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ: According to the means of the poor
key_terms.عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ: According to the means of the wealthy
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: Provision or gift given to a divorced woman

ai.seo_question: When and how much provision is a divorced woman entitled to receive from her ex-husband according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the 'muta' (gift) for divorced women is bestowed after the completion of the waiting period (iddah), distinguishing it from maintenance during that time. It underscores the principle of proportional provision based on financial capacity, citing the exemplary practice of Imam Hasan ibn Ali, who consistently gifted a slave woman to his divorced wives, thereby establishing a high standard for the wealthy.
